ex: Det är svårt att hitta en {bostad} i Stockholm.
exEn: It's hard to find a place to live in Stockholm.
note: Plural with a vowel change: bostäder. Bostadsbrist = housing shortage.

exEn: How much is the rent?
note: Rent is normally paid in advance, before the month starts.

ex: Hon {hyr} ett rum hos en äldre dam.
exEn: She rents a room from an elderly lady.
note: Present tense hyr, not hyrer. Hyra ut = to rent out.

exEn: Contact the landlord if something breaks.
note: Often a housing company rather than a person. Värd = host.

exEn: The tenants got a letter from the landlord.
note: Gäst = guest; the g is soft, like j. Hyresgästföreningen is the tenants' union.

ex: Läs {hyreskontraktet} noga innan du skriver under.
exEn: Read the lease carefully before you sign.
note: Kontrakt is stressed on the second syllable: kon-TRAKT. A lease directly with the landlord is a förstahandskontrakt.

ex: Hon har bara ett {andrahandskontrakt} på lägenheten.
exEn: She only has a sublease on the apartment.
note: Hyra i andra hand = to sublet. The landlord usually has to approve it.

exEn: Do you live in a rental or a co-op apartment?
note: An apartment you rent and can't sell. Compare bostadsrätt, which you buy.

exEn: They bought a co-op apartment in Södermalm.
note: You buy the right to live there and pay a monthly fee (avgift) to the housing association.

ex: De bor i en {villa} med stor trädgård.
exEn: They live in a house with a big yard.
note: False friend: a villa is any ordinary detached house, not a luxury home.

ex: Vi har köpt ett {radhus} utanför stan.
exEn: We've bought a townhouse outside town.
note: Rad = row. Same form in the plural: två radhus.

exEn: The apartment is sixty square meters.
note: Written kvm or m² in housing ads. Same form in the plural: sextio kvadratmeter.

ex: Jag har stått i {bostadskön} i fem år.
exEn: I've been in the housing queue for five years.
note: In the big cities people often queue for many years to get a rental apartment.

ex: Kan du hjälpa mig med {flytten} på lördag?
exEn: Can you help me with the move on Saturday?
note: The noun of flytta. Tell Skatteverket about a move with a flyttanmälan.

ex: Vi {flyttar in} i den nya lägenheten i maj.
exEn: We're moving into the new apartment in May.
note: The particle is stressed: flytta IN. Flytta ut = to move out; flytta ihop = to move in together.

exEn: We've packed twenty moving boxes.
note: Kartong = cardboard box. The rt merges into one retroflex sound.

exEn: The notice must be in writing.
note: Uppsägningstid = notice period, usually three months for a rental apartment. From säga upp.

exEn: Is electricity included in the rent?
note: Short for elektricitet. Elräkning = electricity bill.

exEn: The heating isn't working in the bedroom.
note: Also heat or warmth in general: solens värme.

exEn: Have you paid the bills?
note: At a restaurant you ask for notan, not räkningen.

exEn: The fee is four thousand kronor a month.
note: The g is soft, like j. In a bostadsrätt you pay a monthly avgift instead of rent.

exEn: Does the insurance pay for the damage?
note: Stress on the second syllable: för-SÄK-ring. The rs merges into one sh-like sound.

exEn: Everyone should have home insurance.
note: Covers your belongings and usually travel too. Almost every household in Sweden has one.

ex: Jag har bokat {tvättstugan} på torsdag kväll.
exEn: I've booked the laundry room for Thursday evening.
note: The shared laundry room in an apartment building. You book a time slot (tvättid) in advance.

exEn: The garbage room is in the courtyard.
note: The definite form doubles the m: soprummet.

exEn: Can you take out the trash?
note: Plural only in this sense. A garbage can is en soptunna.

exEn: Where can I throw away old batteries?
note: The everyday word for throwing things away. Kasta is to throw (a ball).

ex: Vi lämnar glas och tidningar på {återvinningen}.
exEn: We take glass and newspapers to the recycling station.
note: In everyday speech återvinningen often means the recycling station (återvinningsstation).

ex: Grannarna {stör} oss med hög musik varje helg.
exEn: The neighbors disturb us with loud music every weekend.
note: Present tense stör, not störer. Förlåt att jag stör! = Sorry to bother you!

exEn: What's your address?
note: Spelled with one d: adress.

exEn: Has the mail come yet?
note: Can also mean the postal service: skicka något med posten. Email is mejl.

ex: Det kom ett {brev} till dig idag.
exEn: A letter came for you today.
note: Same form in the plural: två brev. A letter of the alphabet is en bokstav.

ex: Jag ska hämta ut ett {paket} i affären.
exEn: I'm going to pick up a package at the store.
note: Stress on the second syllable: pa-KET. Hämta ut = to collect (a parcel).

ex: Jag fick en {avi} om att paketet har kommit.
exEn: I got a notice that the package has arrived.
note: Often a text message saying where to collect a parcel; bring ID. A hyresavi is a rent invoice.

exEn: Have you checked the mailbox today?
note: Both your own mailbox and the yellow public box for sending letters.

exEn: There's a signature missing on the form.
note: From skriva under (to sign). The rs merges into one sh-like sound.

ex: Du måste {skriva under} här och här.
exEn: You need to sign here and here.
note: The particle under is stressed. Skriva på means the same: skriva på kontraktet.

ex: Du kan ladda ner {blanketten} på hemsidan.
exEn: You can download the form from the website.
note: False friend: a blanket is en filt. An online form is usually called formulär.

en: to fill in; to fill out
exEn: Fill in your name and personal ID number.
note: The particle i is stressed and long: fyll I. Fylla alone means to fill.

ex: Man måste kontakta många {myndigheter} när man flyttar hit.
exEn: You have to contact lots of agencies when you move here.
note: Many agencies end in -verket or -kassan: Skatteverket, Migrationsverket, Försäkringskassan. The g is often silent.

exEn: Can I have your personal ID number?
note: Your date of birth plus four digits: YYMMDD-XXXX. You need it almost everywhere. Definite: personnumret.

exEn: Once you're registered, you get a personal ID number.
note: Registered at an address = folkbokförd, in everyday speech skriven: Var är du skriven?

exEn: Can I see your ID?
note: Usually shortened to leg: Har du leg? A passport, an ID card or a Swedish driver's license all count.

ex: Du kan beställa ett {id-kort} hos Skatteverket.
exEn: You can order an ID card from the Tax Agency.
note: Also written ID-kort. Skatteverket issues them to people registered (folkbokförda) in Sweden.

ex: Hyresvärden vill se att du har en fast {inkomst}.
exEn: The landlord wants to see that you have a steady income.
note: Many landlords ask for an income of about three times the rent.

ex: Hur mycket {skatt} betalar man i Sverige?
exEn: How much tax do you pay in Sweden?
note: Skatt also means treasure. Skatteverket = the Swedish Tax Agency.

ex: {Deklarationen} ska vara inne i början av maj.
exEn: The tax return is due at the beginning of May.
note: To file your tax return = deklarera. Most people just approve it online with BankID.

ex: Jag behöver ett {intyg} från min arbetsgivare.
exEn: I need a certificate from my employer.
note: Läkarintyg = doctor's certificate. Same form in the plural: två intyg.

exEn: She has been granted a residence permit in Sweden.
note: Issued by Migrationsverket. A permanent residence permit is often called PUT.

exEn: He has applied for Swedish citizenship.
note: A citizen is en medborgare. The g in -borgar- sounds like j.
